title: Edge-exchange Gray codes for directed spanning trees
formal: For every finite loopless simple directed graph and root r admitting an out-arborescence, do all spanning out-arborescences admit an arc-exchange listing?
definitions: A directed graph has a finite nonempty vertex set V and arcs (u,v) with u≠v, at most one arc for each ordered pair; opposite arcs may both occur. The root r∈V is fixed. An out-arborescence is an arc set of size |V|−1 in which r has indegree zero, every other vertex has indegree one, and every vertex is reachable from r along chosen arcs. The graph is promised to contain at least one such set. A listing contains every such arc set exactly once, and consecutive sets differ by deleting one arc and inserting one other arc. There is no last-to-first requirement and no bound on computation. The one-vertex case has the single empty arborescence.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the universal listing proposition or a counterexample and nonexistence proof.
context: Problem 2 is the directed question. Replacing each undirected edge by its two orientations makes a positive answer imply the undirected pivot-exchange statement.
why: This extends minimal-change enumeration to rooted directed connectivity and implies the undirected pivot-exchange existence statement.

import_provenance.original_title: Edge-exchange Gray codes for directed spanning trees
import_provenance.original_statement: For every directed graph and fixed root, can all spanning arborescences directed away from that root be listed so that successive arborescences exchange exactly one arc? This is Knuth’s directed spanning-tree Gray-code problem, presented alongside the authors’ undirected results.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The directed question is stronger than the preceding undirected question; they are distinct models of the same enumeration programme.

sentences: The root is fixed before listing directed spanning trees.
Every listed tree must orient all paths away from that root.
Successive trees delete one arc and insert one arc.
The endpoints of the full list need not be adjacent.
This directed statement would imply the related undirected pivot-exchange statement.
